newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy shares end down but off lows, Wall St weighs.
newsitem.headline: Italy shares end down but off lows, Wall St weighs.

text.p: Italian shares closed easier but off session lows on Wednesday in a market depressed by Wall Street's performance, giving up most of the gains made in the previous session.
"It was a speculative session today," one trader said, noting underlying sentiment remained positive but the market lacked the impetus to make a move up.
The all-share Mibtel index ended 0.64 percent down at 10,478 after a 10,449 to 10,500 range while the Mib30 blue chip index closed 0.83 percent lower at 15,660 after a 15,607-15,707 range.

Traded volume was only moderate, estimated at around 555 billion lire after some 660 billion lire on Tuesday, in a very selective market with selling seen mainly by domestic investors but with some foreign buy orders.
Fiat showed a marked improvement in afternoon business, closing 1.86 percent up at 4,440 lire as rumours resurfaced of possible government incentives to boost the depressed Italian car market.
But insurer Generali was down 1.94 percent at 30,166 lire as rumours again emerged of a possible acquisition of insurance company SAI which rose 4.31 percent to 13,758.

Telecoms were mixed but mobile phone operator TIM put on 0.75 percent to 3,626 lire on foreign buying after its managing director Vito Gamberale said it had asked the Posts ministry for authorisation to offer a DECT cordless phone service.

Its sister company Telecom Italia, off 0.75 percent at 3,576, has already announced plans to launch an advanced cordless phone using the DECT standard. Telecoms holding group Stet was 1.22 percent down at 6,457.
Pirelli & C holding pared gains to end 2.42 percent up at 1,907 while Pirelli SpA ended 0.53 percent off at 2,839 after market talk of a group restructuring, denied by Pirelli.
